## Natural history notes

A small shining leaf chafer beetle characterized by its oval body, tan to brownish coloration, and subtle darker markings or wavy patterning on the wing covers. In Florida, it is found in sandy or open habitats such as pine flatwoods, scrub, fields, lawns, roadsides, and forest edges where adults may feed on foliage or flowers. Adults are often active at night and may come to lights, while the larvae develop underground as white grubs that feed on roots or decaying organic matter, helping move plant material through the soil food web.
